newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firmer on mildly bullish API data.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firmer on mildly bullish API data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil and gas oil futures opened firmer in line with market expectations on Wednesday after the overnight release of mildly bullish weekly stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API), traders said.

June Brent stood at $18.18 a barrel at 0942 GMT, 19 cents up on the day, after closing 35 cents a barrel lower on Tuesday because of a sharp sell-off in New York ahead of the expiry of the May NYMEX crude oil contract.
IPE gas oil was a dollar firmer at $164.75 a tonne.
"It is the APIs, we are now at the levels we had expected before the open...there is not a great deal of other news around," one IPE dealer said.
The API report showed a 4.7 million barrel draw on the middle distillates, compared with expectations of a half-million barrel decline.
The report also revised downwards by 3.1 million barrels its assessment in its previous report of gasoline inventories.
The revised figures showed a seasonal 1.9 million barrel drawdown in gasoline stocks in the week to April 18, compared to the previous week.

Traders and technical analysts said the market's test of, but failure convincingly to break into, an upside gap on the charts between $18.62 and $18.77 on Tuesday, was a bearish signal. Support at the year's low weighs in at $17.61, they added.
"We have established a range between about $17.60 and $18.60 and we are in the middle of that," one IPE dealer said.
